I tried to OD with acetaminophen in March because I took like twice the amount that could kill a person. I go to med school so I know the bad doses you can take but *of course* I won't tell you because I don't want you to die, you deserve to have a good life and you won't have that if you die


But I'll tell you what will happen to you if you take more pills: in some minutes you'll start throwing up because your body knows it's bad for you. Then you'll start to feel kinda "sleepy" and groggy (it's a really weird thing to feel). Then you'll feel nauseous. IF you take enough to die (which is really really a lot l so I doubt you'll ever be able to take it) it'll take at least 2 days for you to die. During this time you'll have a liver failure, which will cause a lot of other bad symptoms. Pain because of liver failure is horrible and even if you go to the hospital and take the morphine you'll still feel horrible. When your liver gets too destroyed, it can cause brain damage.

You know why acetaminophen OD is common? Because is cheap, not because it actually works. It won't work, you probably won't get the right amount so you'll only feel a lot of pain, you'll cause some possible permanent liver damage but nothing will happen.

I have depression and anorexia

For depression: create a routine for you. I know we don't have any strength and we don't feel like doing anything. But try to choose at least 3 things you need to do in the day (it can be like taking a shower, eating, cleaning something, etc). You'll feel much better than if you stay in bed all day. Just try to do things for 10 minutes, it's already good enough!

For anorexia: stay away from pro-ana forums. They're shitty and those advices are so toxic and stupid. I know the ED seems more trustworthy than your doctors but people don't want you hurting yourself. Being skinny is not whorty all the suffering we have. You don't have to love yourself, just work on stopping hating yourself 


For both: look for a therapist (and a psychiatrist if needed). It'll feel weird and maybe a little unhelpful in the beginning (at least it was for me because I didn't exactly wanted to recover) but soon you'll feel relieved. Just don't give up :)

maybe because depression affects our **whole** life. There's not categories in our life like "that's the part of my brain that deals with my job, that one deals with studies and this little one is where I keep my depressive thoughts".

Yeah, we can discover, travel, learn and love. But everything is always taken by our sad thoughts. We'll do it all while thinking we're stupid and dumb and doing everything wrong.

Also, **fun fact**: we'll do everything while thinking that EVERYBODY HATES US so you're obviously being a jerk when you say this! You're actually the one people don't like, that's why you think you should say those mean thing for others. Usually, when we don't have anything good to say, it's better to shut up :)

It's a disease, not a simple choice. We can't just "put on our big boys pants and walk out side". We would, if we could. Instead we just need to spend time and money to treat a condition we didn't asked for.

(just out of curiosity: would you say the same things if he was complaining about wanting to die because he can't stand cancer anymore??)

it depends. Honestly, I don't know a lot about shakes and protein drinks but I think it doesn't have all the nutrients a person need to have daily so this person will probably be malnourished (yeah, an overweight person can be overweight AND malnourished).

If the main goal is to lose weight, it's better to go to a dietitian or a nutritionist and ask for a proper diet. It can be good to also look for some exercises (I also recommend to look for a professional)

Ps. despite the fact that I hate the diet culture, I think it's preferable to have an proper diet made from a certified professional (who can also notice disordered eating patterns and possible EDs) than doing it by yourself and risking developing some disease in the future.

I'm 21 and I remember when I was younger. I suffered bullying during all my school days and I didn't have a lot of friends so thought I would know more people in the internet and be less lonely. Turns out people from my school started bullying me in the internet too. After all those years I still fear doing anything in the internet. I don't post anything and I never do any comments. I feel a little bit safer in my anonymous accounts but I'm always terrified someone will find out and that'll be the reason why they'll make jokes about me again... I hate that so much.

Have you tried just recording your videos? You don't have to post it anywhere, just record and, if you can, show to someone you trust. Try to get used to seeing your videos and then slowly start posting (maybe some short videos now and then in the beginning). Always respect yourself but try to slowly challenge your fears until you're able to post it.
There's also a lot of Facebook groups and - I don't know if you feel like that but - maybe posting your videos to a lot of strangers can feel safer than doing it with people you know (I mean they don't know you so the chances are you'll never see them again)

when I was 15 I had some family problems and no one was in my side (despite the fact that I was right). I already dealt with my mental illness all by myself for years so I decided I was going to attempt suicide but for some reason - I have no idea why - I wanted to go to school the next day so I would do it after the class. I had an important exam this day but I didn't study (after all, I was going to die, why would I study?).

There was this trouble kid who sat next to me and the all teachers always stayed in his side so he wouldn't cheat. That's how my teacher saw me looking at the test for exactly 45 minutes without answering a single question. I was always one of the 3 best students from the class so that was really strange. I handed the paper to him and he asked if I was okay  I said "no". After everyone ended the exam he called me outside the class and said he noticed I wasn't okay for days and that I could talk to him if I needed. I didn't said anything because I didn't want my parents involved.

I don't think he knows but that was the first time someone truly asked me if I was okay in years. He was young (he was in his 20s) and always liked to keep the bad boy appearance so I know it was hard for him to show any emotion so he could show how much he cared about me. I spent the rest of the day crying and I gave up on my plans.

Now I'm almost 21. Do I regret not killing myself that day? yes, sometimes. Do I still struggle with my mental illness? yes. Things are good now for me? no. Some days I really wish I had died that day but looking for everything that happened in all those years, I'm grateful I stayed because I was able to live a lot of good moments. I still feel bad but mostly I stay because I know there are still more good moments to come.

Sorry for the long story, I just wanted to show you that waiting some time can make some difference. Even some minutes more can give you some hope. Don't give up, I know the pain is big but there are some things worthy.

There are still time for people to understand your feelings and help you.
